summary: A farmer's grown son runs the family farm while the father campaigns for the legislature.
realLife: A Nebraska legislature profile of a state senator said his son ran the family farm while the senator was campaigning. The couple has two children, the son on the farm and a daughter serving as an Air Force captain. The profile does not say how the farm is handled once he serves.
gates: The candidate owns or runs a family business such as a farm.
A grown child lives near and works in the business.
The candidate has filed for office.
weights: Whether the son wants the farm.
How much the business needs the candidate's own work.
inGame: Jobs and pay, a family business, kin ties between parent and adult child and a candidate's filing could carry it; a family farm handed to a relative needs a business role record held by a kin member.

turns.what: No relative can run the farm, so the candidate hires a manager or scales back.
turns.pulledBy: No adult children nearby, a busy season.

turns.what: The son keeps the farm after the term and the father never returns to it.
turns.writesBack: Business ownership moves to the son; father's job ended.

turns.what: The candidate and son split the work, with the candidate back at harvest.
turns.pulledBy: A short session, a seasonal business.
turns.writesBack: Shared business roles; candidate's hours cut.
